subject: Reliability banding and credit trigger model for monthly SLA
messages:
From: Priya Singh <procurement@uptownhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Anand Rao <anand@uptownhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template: uptime targets & monthly credit model

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — Uptown's product and performance profile look promising. As we start legal/procurement, attached is our preferred SLA language and an internal spreadsheet with target availability we need to align on. High level asks:

- Standard monthly uptime target we must see in contract: 99.95% (regional measurement).
- Clear monthly credit formula tied to minutes of unavailability with a 50% cap on credits for the billing period.
- We'd like latency carveouts removed (i.e., no separate latency credits), but we will accept operational commitments on p95/p99 for critical APIs.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept the 99.95% baseline and a 50% cap? If not, what would be your suggested compromise that still meets our risk profile?

Attaching our procurement sheet: uptown_procurement_requirements.xlsx

We'd prefer a short call to resolve this — Anand and I are available Tuesday afternoon.

Thanks,
Priya Singh

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime targets & monthly credit model

Hi Priya — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful.

Short answer: we can work toward a 99.95% baseline in US regions, but to protect predictable economics and operational behavior we propose a graded credit-trigger model rather than a flat minutes-to-credit approach. Proposed high-level compromise:

1) Regional baseline uptime: US 99.95%, EU 99.90% (measured per-region on a monthly rolling basis).
2) Graded credit bands (monthly bill credits applied to the affected region only):
   - Degraded (cumulative unavailable minutes > 15 min within a 24h window): 5% credit for the month
   - Major degradation (cumulative unavailable minutes > 120 min within the month): 20% credit for the month
   - Outage (total monthly availability < 95% for the region): 50% credit for the month
3) Latency: commit to p95 < 120ms and p99 < 450ms for the public inference API; latency credits only trigger for sustained degradation (continuous 15+ minutes where p99 > 2x target) to avoid crediting for short spikes.
4) Cap: we can accept a 50% monthly credit cap for extreme outages, but we'd like a contractual exception for scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified) and force majeure.
5) Measurement & remediation: Redwood will publish per-region availability dashboards and provide a remediation timeline with root-cause writeup for any credit-triggering event.

I've attached a redline (uptown_sla_redlines_v1.pdf) that encodes the above language and shows one alternative: a fixed-minute-to-credit mapping that you can review.

Ben — can you confirm the practical thresholds for measuring "unavailable minutes" (how we count requests in flight, partial routing failovers vs hard outages) so I can set expectations clearly? Marcus, looping you for legal flags on the measurement and cap language.

If this structure is acceptable, I propose a 30-minute call to iron out the measurement definition and DocuSign the updated SLA addendum. Link to a proposed DocuSign envelope below.

Next steps: pick a 30-min window Tue/Wed, confirm internal contacts for post-incident reports, and review redline.

Best,

Subject: RE: SLA template: uptime targets & monthly credit model

Grace / team — quick technical note to support the proposed banding:

- Measurement: we'll use region-scoped request success rates aggregated into 1-minute buckets. A minute is considered "unavailable" for the region if aggregate request success < 99% for that minute for the API surface in-scope.
- Partial routing/gradual degradation: we'll treat full-region unavailability separately from degraded availability due to capacity (that is why graded bands are important). For capacity-driven degradation, we'd evaluate trailing 1-hour windows and require a 15-minute sustained threshold before crediting.
- Latency: p95/p99 measured on production traffic using our telemetry (client-observed latencies). For credit triggers we need sustained violations (>=15 continuous minutes) so short spikes don't trigger credits.
- Data sources: Redwood metrics (public dashboard) + ability to share raw minute-level CSVs under NDA for disputed events. Attached a small sample of how the minute buckets look: regional-latency-metrics.csv

This approach keeps the incentives aligned: we remediate severe incidents quickly and avoid crediting customers for transient noise. Happy to walk through a sample calculation on the call.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Priya / Anand — thanks for the quick back-and-forth and for sharing the procurement sheet. Below is a concise summary of the proposal we can put into the SLA addendum (redline attached). Please reply with confirmation or suggested edits so we can finalize the DocuSign: 

Summary (what Redwood proposes)
- Regional baselines: US 99.95%, EU 99.90% (monthly, region-scoped).
- Graded monthly credit model (region-specific): Degraded >15m => 5% credit; Major >120m => 20% credit; Outage <95% availability => 50% credit (per-region).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <120ms, p99 <450ms; latency credits only for sustained p99 > 2x target for >=15 continuous minutes.
- Cap: 50% maximum monthly credit for the affected region; scheduled maintenance (with 72h notice) and force majeure excluded.
- Measurement & evidence: Redwood dashboard + per-minute CSV export on request; remediation timeline and RCA within 7 business days for credit-triggering events.

Attachments: uptown_sla_redlines_v1.pdf (redline including billing language), regional-latency-metrics.csv (sample buckets), uptown_procurement_requirements.xlsx (your original).

If this structure looks acceptable, next steps:
1) Priya — confirm acceptance of the banding model and measurement definition, or propose edits inline by EOD Wed.
2) We schedule a 30-min call (Ben will walk through sample calculations).
3) Redwood to issue DocuSign with the SLA addendum once legal confirms result (Marcus).
